rationale: nsieve-bits is a tiny (521 text bytes, single hot 'main') compute-kernel dominated by tight bit-manipulation and sieve loops, so runtime cost is the binding constraint and size cost a secondary one: BCF and FLA carry the highest RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights so the selector applies them only where feature scores strongly justify it (or skips the hottest loops), while SUB is favored because arithmetic/bitwise substitution is cheap, low-risk, and directly obscures the sieve's bitwise logic; SPLIT is cheap and amplifies the effectiveness of control-flow passes on a single large function so it gets high diversity weight with minimal penalties; IBR is moderately weighted as a control-flow hardener that pairs well with FLA but is held back by per-branch dispatch overhead in hot loops; ICALL and IGV are down-weighted because with only 2 functions, minimal call sites, and negligible global-variable structure they offer little security or diversity benefit while adding indirect-call and correctness risk.
